npcs.name: Sir Bors de Ganis
npcs.idle: Percival will march when someone gives him the word. Until then, the Lake's knights hold the merchants, and I hold Percival.

npcs.name: Lunete of the Lake
npcs.idle: My Lady sleeps under the water. She does not sleep well, with Morgana on her shore.

npcs.name: Nest ferch Rhys
npcs.idle: Have you heard them? At night? Don't listen if you do.

npcs.name: Gwion the Harper
npcs.idle: Every song in this valley ends in the lake. I've tried to write one that doesn't.

npcs.name: Brother Teilo
npcs.idle: Every brother in my house is dead and still walking. I am the only one who stayed dead-tired instead.

quests.title: The Diamondbacks
quests.offer:
Diamondback toads on the north shore - big as ponies, and they spit. They never came out of the shallows before Morgana came. Now they sit on the road.

Will you [clear the shore]?
quests.summary: Diamondback toads have come up out of the shallows onto Llyn Barfog's north shore.

steps.goal: Kill the diamondback toads about 350 m north of Sir Bors de Ganis
Tell Sir Bors
steps.say: Good. The road's open - and now you've seen the north shore, you've seen why we can't hold it yet.

default.text: From the Knights of the Lake.

quests.title: The Afanc's Brood
quests.offer:
Arthur dragged the Afanc out of this lake with chains and oxen, and that was the end of it - so the story goes. Then why are there afanc hatchlings on the north shore?

Something is breeding them. Will you [find out what]?
quests.summary: Afanc hatchlings are breeding on Llyn Barfog's north shore - and the Afanc was killed long ago.

steps.goal: Kill the afanc hatchlings about 290 m north of Sir Bors de Ganis
Search Carn March Arthur, the hoof-stone in the northern hills

clue.name: a stone with a hoof-print, under a red chain

steps.text: Arthur's horse left its hoof-print here when he dragged the Afanc out. Someone has chained a Crimson ward-stone over the print, and written on it: 'What the King took out, the Queen puts back.'

steps.goal: Tell Sir Bors
steps.say: 'What the King took out, the Queen puts back.' She's raising the Afanc. Gods. Percival needs to hear this.

default.text: From the Knights of the Lake.

quests.title: The Ward on the Shore
quests.offer:
The Crimson keep a post on the Afanc's shore, and a gatekeeper who chains wards over every stone Arthur ever touched. Break him and the shore is ours to march on.

It's not a one-sword job. Will you [break the post]?
quests.summary: A Crimson gatekeeper keeps Morgana's post on the Afanc's shore.

steps.goal: Defeat the Crimson gatekeeper on the Afanc's shore
steps.text: The gatekeeper falls across his own ward-stones, and the red chains go slack.

stages.name: Gatekeeper Hywel Redkey
stages.announce: A man in crimson with a ring of red keys steps out of the post: 'Every door has a keeper. This one's mine.'

steps.goal: Tell Sir Bors
steps.say: The ward's broken. Now when the Host marches, it has a shore to stand on. Percival thanks you - I thank you louder.

default.text: From the Knights of the Lake.

quests.title: The Hounds of Annwn
quests.offer:
My husband Iolo heard the hounds of Annwn three nights ago. The white hounds with red ears. Whoever hears them dies within the year - everybody knows that.

Iolo isn't one to wait for it. He took his spear and went to hunt them, to break the doom. Gwion the [harper] knows the old stories. Will you [go after Iolo]?

topics.harper: Gwion. He sits by the smithy, playing to anyone who'll stand still.

quests.summary: Iolo heard the hounds of Annwn - a death omen - and went to hunt them rather than wait to die.

steps.goal: Ask Gwion the harper about the hounds
steps.say: The Cwn Annwn hunt from the old stones south of here, on the slopes. Their master is a huntsman of the Otherworld. The story goes, if a living man blows the huntsman's horn, the hunt passes him by - but the doom must fall on someone. They always find someone. Iolo will go to the [stones].

steps.goal: Hunt the hounds of Annwn on the slopes
steps.text: They don't bleed. They fade, like breath on cold glass. Further south, a horn calls.

steps.goal: Search the old stones in the south
steps.text: Iolo's spear, the shaft bitten through. A trail of blood to the west - and the hunt's horn calling again, very close.

steps.goal: Defeat the huntsman of Annwn
steps.text: The huntsman lowers his horn and looks at you a long while. Then he and his hounds are gone, and only the horn lies on the grass.

stages.name: Gwyn's Huntsman
stages.announce: A tall grey figure rides out of nothing on a horse of mist, the white hounds at its heels. It lifts a horn.

steps.goal: Find Iolo
steps.say:
You came for me? Nest sent you. Course she did.

I heard it, you know. In the howling. My own name. They've marked me. I'm marked. Unless the [horn]...

steps.goal: Decide what to do with the horn
steps.say:
If I blow it, the hunt passes me by - and the doom falls on whoever's near. On you, maybe. I won't do that.

If YOU [blow it], it falls on you. Gods, don't. Or we [break it], and I take what's coming. A year. A year is something.

options.say:
No - you - ...

Listen. They're going. Far off. They're running the other way. They know your name now, friend. I'm sorry. I'm so sorry, and so grateful I can't stand up.
Yes. Yes. A year with Nest. That's more than most men get. Come on, help me up.

steps.goal: Bring Iolo home to Nest
steps.say:
He's home, and he says the doom is gone - and he won't tell me where it went.

I can guess. Thank you. I don't know what else to say. Take this. Be careful at night.

steps.goal: Bring Iolo home to Nest
steps.say:
A year. He told me. He broke the horn and he chose a year with me, and he's smiling like a boy about it.

I'll make it the best year of his life. Here. For bringing him home to have it.

blown.text: Take this. Be careful at night.

quests.title: Master of the Hunt
quests.offer:
Gwyn's huntsman was one rider of the hunt. The hunt's MASTER rides the western shore now - the Huntsman of Annwn, Morgana's own, with his pack. While he rides, every night in this valley is a doom for someone.

This needs a group, and courage. Will you [end the hunt]?
quests.summary: The Huntsman of Annwn, master of Morgana's hounds, rides Llyn Barfog's western shore.

steps.goal: Bring down the Huntsman of Annwn about 620 m west of Gwion the Harper
Tell Gwion the Harper
steps.say:
No horn tonight. No horn for a long while.

I'll write it. A song about the valley that doesn't end in the lake. You've given me the ending.

quests.title: The Lady's Cattle
quests.offer:
Do you know why this is the bearded lake? A maiden came up out of it with white cattle, and gave them to the farmers of the valley - and when a greedy man would have slaughtered one, she called them home under the water.

The bwgan have driven off the last of her herd, to feed Morgana's hounds. Will you [find the herd]?
quests.summary: The bwgan of the north-west hills have driven off the Lady of the Lake's white cattle to feed Morgana's hounds.

steps.goal: Drive off the bwgan hunters about 540 m north-west of Lunete of the Lake
Search the bwgan pens

clue.name: a broken pen, white hairs caught on the rails

steps.text: Empty. White hairs on every rail, and tracks going north into the hills - big tracks, bigger than any bwgan's, walking beside the cattle.

steps.goal: Tell Lunete of the Lake
steps.say: North, into the hills. With something big walking beside them. I know who that is. Everyone in this valley knows who that is.

default.text: From the Maidens of the Lake.

quests.title: Up Through the Gate
quests.offer:
The cythraul are Annwn's - demons of the deep places. They come up through Morgana's gate a few at a time, and walk the bwgan hills looking for anything alive.

Will you [send them back]?
quests.summary: Cythraul, demons of Annwn, come up through Morgana's gate and walk Llyn Barfog's north-west hills.

steps.goal: Send the cythraul back about 460 m north-west of Lunete of the Lake
Tell Lunete of the Lake
steps.say: Back where they came from. My Lady felt every one go. She says thank you, which she does not say often.

default.text: From the Maidens of the Lake.

quests.title: The King of the Barfog Hills
quests.offer:
The King of the Barfog Hills. He's no king - a great beast of the northern hills that calls itself one - but Morgana has bought him with the Lady's own cattle, and he keeps the last white cow in his den.

It's a fight for a group. Will you [bring her home]?
quests.summary: The King of the Barfog Hills keeps the Lady of the Lake's last white cow in his den in the northern hills.

steps.goal: Bring down the King of the Barfog Hills about 560 m north of Lunete of the Lake
Tell Lunete of the Lake
steps.say: She's alive? The last of them. I can [call her home], under the water, where Morgana can't reach her - and the valley will never see the white cattle again. Or she can go to [the farmers], to Gwartheg Yllyn at the east gate, and the herd can begin again on the land, the way my Lady meant it.

options.say: Then she goes home. Listen - you'll hear her bell under the water on still nights.
Then the valley has its cattle again. My Lady will be glad - she always liked farmers better than kings.

home.text: From the Maidens of the Lake.

farm.text: From the Maidens of the Lake.

quests.title: The Last Psalm
quests.offer:
I'm the last brother of the abbey in the north - the last living one. Thirty years ago our abbot made a pact with the ghosts of an old legion: they would guard our house from raiders. They did. They guarded it from everything.

This winter my brothers died one by one, and rose again, and went back to their prayers. I ran. I am not proud of it. Will you [go to the abbey]? The abbot's psalter holds the pact. Perhaps it holds a way out.
quests.summary: Brother Teilo's abbey made a pact with the ghosts of a Roman legion, and now his dead brothers walk.

steps.goal: Climb the road to the abbey in the north
steps.text: The abbey bell is ringing for vespers. Hooded monks walk the cloister in pairs. None of them cast a shadow.

steps.goal: Free the dead brothers of the abbey
steps.text: Each one says 'thank you' as it falls.

steps.goal: Find the abbot's psalter

clue.name: a chained psalter on a lectern

steps.text: The pact is written in the margin of the psalm for the dead: 'Guard this house until the last brother leaves it.' And Teilo left.

steps.goal: Speak with the ghost of Abbot Elfodd
steps.say:
You have the psalter. Good. I made the pact. I meant it for our protection. The legion took it to the letter, as soldiers do - the last brother left, so the house is theirs, and so are we.

Their veteran, Decimus, holds the pact. Break him, and I can [read the last psalm].

steps.goal: Defeat Decimus, keeper of the pact
steps.text: The old soldier salutes you as he fades. 'Relieved. At last.'

stages.name: Evocatus Decimus
stages.announce: An old soldier in a red cloak plants himself in the cloister. 'This house is under guard. Stand down.'

steps.goal: Choose with the abbot
steps.say:
Now I can read it - the last psalm, and every brother here goes to his rest, myself among them. The abbey will stand empty, and the raiders will come, and the valley will have no one to shelter it.

Or we [keep watch], the dead brothers and I, without the legion - and the valley keeps its shelter. Teilo would have to live with that. Tell me: do I [read the psalm]?

options.say: Then listen. ... It's been a long time since I could hear myself sing.
Then we watch. Tell Teilo we are not angry. Tell him to visit, if he can bear it.

steps.goal: Return to Brother Teilo
steps.say:
I heard them. All the way down here. Singing - all of them, the old psalm. And then the bell stopped.

I'll go back in the spring and sweep the chapel. Somebody should.

steps.goal: Return to Brother Teilo
steps.say:
They're keeping watch. Still. Without the legion.

I'll visit. I'll bring bread they can't eat and news they can't use. I suppose that's what brothers are for.

quests.title: The Legion of the Pact
quests.offer:
The abbot's pact is broken, one way or the other - but the legion's dead didn't all go with Decimus. Some still march round the abbey walls, and they've begun stopping travellers on the north road.

Will you [relieve the watch]? Soldiers like to be relieved.
quests.summary: The dead legionaries of the abbey's broken pact still march round its walls and stop travellers on the north road.

steps.goal: Relieve the legionaries of the pact about 720 m north-east of Brother Teilo
Tell Brother Teilo
steps.say: Relieved. That's the word Decimus used, isn't it? I hope it's the word they all use.

quests.title: The Still Night
quests.offer:
The Crimson in the bwgan hills carry letters to and from the Gate. If we knew what Morgana waits for, we'd know how long we have.

Will you [take a letter]?
quests.summary: Crimson acolytes carry Morgana's letters between the bwgan hills and the Gate of Annwn.

steps.goal: Kill the crimson acolytes carrying letters about 460 m north-west of Lunete of the Lake
Search the Crimson post for letters

clue.name: a red satchel under a bedroll

steps.text: One letter, in Morgana's own hand: 'The Gate opens on the night the lake is still. The Afanc wakes first. Mordred walks second. Then I walk Annwn's dead into Camelot.'

steps.goal: Bring the letter to Lunete of the Lake
steps.say:
The night the lake is still. It's never still - my Lady keeps it moving, every night, to keep that gate shut. She's tiring.

So we haven't long. Percival has to march.

default.text: From the Maidens of the Lake.

quests.title: The Fay Wood
quests.offer:
Morgana is a fay - half of her is - and the Ellyll of the south-west wood are her kin. Her fay knights ride out of that wood in green steel, and cut down anything that comes near the Gate from the west.

A group's work. Will you [ride into the wood]?
quests.summary: Morgana's fay knights ride out of the Ellyll wood in Llyn Barfog's south-west and guard the Gate from the west.

steps.goal: Cut down Morgana's fay knights about 630 m south-west of Sir Bors de Ganis
Tell Sir Bors
steps.say: Green steel and glamour. Strip the glamour and they bleed like anyone. Good.

default.text: From the Knights of the Lake.

quests.title: The Gate-Captain
quests.offer:
Gate-Captain Branwen holds the south shore for Morgana. She chose this - she was a knight of the Lake once, before Morgana made her promises. Whatever the Host does, it does nothing while Branwen holds the shore.

Bring a group. Will you [face Branwen]?
quests.summary: Gate-Captain Branwen, a knight of the Lake turned to Morgana, holds the south shore before the Gate of Annwn.

steps.goal: Defeat Gate-Captain Branwen about 500 m south of Sir Bors de Ganis
Tell Sir Bors
steps.say:
She was a good knight. Better than me, once.

The shore is open. Go and see Lunete - she's been looking at the lake all day, and she won't say why.

default.text: From the Knights of the Lake.

quests.title: The Lady of the Lake
quests.offer:
Come to the shore with me. Near the Gate - not too near. The lake went still at noon, and it hasn't moved since.

My Lady is waiting for you. Will you [come to the shore]?
quests.summary: Llyn Barfog has gone still, and the Lady of the Lake waits on the south shore.

steps.goal: Go to the south shore, near the Gate of Annwn
steps.text: The water is flat as glass. A woman stands on it - not in it, ON it - in white, with water running from her hair. Behind her, on the far shore, the Gate is a black arch, and there is something moving in it.

steps.goal: Hear the Lady of the Lake
steps.say:
(Lunete speaks for her; the Lady's lips do not move.)

'I gave Arthur his sword. I took it back. I held this gate shut for him, and after him, and I am tired. Morgana is my sister in craft, and she will win if no one stands with me.

'Swear to the [sword], and stand with my knights when Percival marches. Or keep [the old ways], and stand with my maidens. Either way - stand.'

options.say: 'Then you are a knight of the Lake, whatever your arms. Go to Percival.'
'Then you are my maidens' friend, whatever your name. Go to Percival - he needs the old ways too.'

sword.text: From the Lady of the Lake. Sir Percival waits at the merchants: give him the word when you're ready to march.

ways.text: From the Lady of the Lake. Sir Percival waits at the merchants: give him the word when you're ready to march.
